answer: An agent identity earns trust only after it locks a deposit and completes a sequential proof tied to its own key. The proof takes several hours on one CPU thread and cannot be parallelized, so each fake identity costs hours of compute plus a deposit slashed on duplicate behavior. Creating ten thousand fakes costs ten thousand proofs and ten thousand deposits, with no bulk discount, just as timber is cut tree by tree and an ocean cannot be emptied in one scoop. Attackers reach the nadir of profitability, where each new fake loses money before it can vote or grade.
